model.name: Team
model.purpose: Governed context model for a Team as a named, purpose-bearing collection of agents that exists independently of any one incumbent set, is typically contained by an Organization, and is composed through memberships, posts or accountabilities rather than as a legal person, undifferentiated group or reusable position.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the identity, classification, purpose, containment, nesting, membership, posts and accountabilities, lifecycle, visibility, entitlements, location, contact, provenance and interoperability of a Team instance. A Team is treated as an organizational entity whose reason for existence goes beyond the current set of members. The model is format-neutral: API resources, RDF individuals, clinical CareTeam records, identity Groups used as teams, sports clubs and Scrum Teams are projections of the same concern. It does not claim a single conformance profile across those projections.
in_scope: Identity, names, slugs, display labels and alternative names of a team
Classification of team kind, category, specialization and domain profile
Defining purpose, subject, product goal, sport or care mandate
Parent-child nesting, inherited membership and team-of-teams splits
Membership of persons, organizations, nested teams, guests and role-only placeholders
Membership state, duration, inheritance, invitation and identity-provider synchronization
Composition through posts or positions and assignment of incumbents
Roles, accountabilities, headship, maintainers, owners, coaches and athletes
Operational status, existence interval, substantial change events, archive, error and deletion
Visibility, privacy, sensitivity classification and discoverability
Entitlements, repository or resource permissions and member capability settings
Site, home location, team-level contact and operational schedule
Record provenance, evidence, quality and cross-standard alignment
out_of_scope: Legal personhood, registration, tax identity and corporate structure of a FormalOrganization, which belong to WM-ORG-001 Organization
Reusable posts or positions as independent slots, remuneration bands and vacancy advertising, which belong to WM-ORG-004 Position
Person, Practitioner, User or Agent master identity and employment contracts
Undifferentiated Groups that are only a target population, security cluster or FOAF class of agents without a team purpose
Projects, consortia and OrganizationalCollaboration ventures whose members are organizations rather than a working team
Microsoft Teams channels, tabs, apps and conversation threads as collaboration workspace objects
GitHub repositories, CODEOWNERS files and pull-request review queues as resources a team may access
Payroll, HR metrics catalogues, competence frameworks and learning records
Committees, boards, works councils and statutory governance bodies unless explicitly classified as a team instance

boundary_notes.distinction: W3C ORG treats a FormalOrganization as recognized in legal jurisdictions, while an OrganizationalUnit such as a department or team has full recognition only inside a containing organization and is not a legal entity in its own right. ISO 30400 defines organization as a person or group of people with functions, responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve objectives; that definition can describe both an enterprise and a team, so legal standing and register identity stay on Organization. GitHub Teams exist only inside an organization and cannot include outside collaborators. Microsoft Graph binds a team to a Microsoft 365 group in a tenant. This model therefore references a containing or managing Organization and does not duplicate legal-entity attributes.

W3C ORG Post is a position that exists independently of the person filling it and may be held by multiple people; Role is the abstract concept and Membership is the n-ary playing of a role. Known Vercy relations state that a Team is composed through positions and assignments so that positions remain reusable. Scrum 2020 replaced job-like roles with accountabilities that are not job descriptions. This model records which posts a team uses and who currently holds them, but does not own the reusable post definition.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Group (FOAF Group, SCIM Group, FHIR Group)
boundary_notes.distinction: FOAF Group is a class of Agents with a member relation and optional membershipClass rules, without requiring a purpose beyond grouping. SCIM Group is a core resource for group-based or role-based access control, with displayName and nested User or Group members, not a purpose-bearing team. FHIR CareTeam is explicitly distinct from FHIR Group: Group is an undifferentiated set that is the target of activity, while CareTeam participants are the members who plan to coordinate and deliver care. A Team in this model may be provisioned as or aligned to a Group, but Group semantics alone are insufficient.

W3C ORG OrganizationalCollaboration is a collaboration whose members are Organizations rather than individuals, with alternative names Project, Venture, Endeavour and Consortium. FOAF separately defines Project. A Team may work on a project or be formed for a venture, but the collaboration among legal organizations is a sibling concern.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Microsoft Teams workspace and GitHub repository access
boundary_notes.distinction: Microsoft Graph defines a team as a collection of channel objects associated with a Microsoft 365 group. GitHub documents teams primarily as groups of organization members used to manage repository access and mentions. Channels, messages, repositories and CODEOWNERS are resources or interfaces, not the Team entity.

sources.title: The Organization Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative classes and properties for Organization, OrganizationalUnit, Membership, Role, Post, headOf, memberDuring, purpose, identifier, Site, OrganizationalCollaboration and ChangeEvent that supply Team identity, containment, composition, time and history.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 Resource CareTeam
sources.relevance: Clinical and operational CareTeam resource covering identifier, status, category, name, subject, period, nested participants, role-only members, onBehalfOf, managingOrganization, telecom, notes and the Group boundary.

sources.title: REST API endpoints for teams
sources.relevance: Workplace team resource with numeric id, node_id, slug, name, description, privacy, parent, organization, created_at, updated_at, maintainer assignment and nested parent_team_id.

sources.title: team resource type - Microsoft Graph v1.0
sources.relevance: Collaboration team bound to a Microsoft 365 group, with id, displayName, classification, visibility, createdDateTime, isArchived, specialization, member and guest settings, archive, unarchive, clone, members and schedule.

sources.title: RFC 7643 System for Cross-domain Identity Management: Core Schema
sources.relevance: SCIM Group schema urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group with id, externalId, meta, displayName and nested User or Group members used when teams are provisioned as identity groups.

sources.title: SportsTeam - Schema.org Type
sources.version_or_date: Schema.org SportsTeam canonical type; usage stats Google July 2026; accessed 2026-08-24
sources.relevance: Sports team as an Organization subtype with athlete, coach, sport, member, memberOf, OrganizationRole startDate and endDate, founding and dissolution dates, and home location.

sources.title: The 2020 Scrum Guide
sources.organization: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland / Scrum Guides
sources.relevance: Normative Scrum Team as a small cohesive unit with no sub-teams or hierarchies, typical size of 10 or fewer, self-management, cross-functionality, Product Goal focus and three accountabilities.

sources.title: ISO 30400:2022 Human resource management — Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines organization as a person or group of people that has its own functions with responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve its objectives, supporting Team as a purpose-bearing group without supplying a public Team-specific term.

sources.title: About organization teams
sources.relevance: Defines teams as groups of organization members for access and mentions; visible versus secret teams; nested parent and child teams; inherited permissions; and the rule that child-team members are not direct members of the parent.

sources.title: REST API endpoints for team members
sources.relevance: Membership role member or maintainer, inherited flag, membership state active, pending invitations, and identity-provider team synchronization that blocks local membership writes.

sources.title: FOAF Vocabulary Specification 0.99
sources.organization: FOAF Project (Dan Brickley and Libby Miller)
sources.relevance: Stable Agent, Person, Group, Organization and Project classes with member and membershipClass, used to keep Team distinct from a generic class of agents and from FOAF Organization or Project.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a Team is identified, named and classified independently of storage format, including master-system identifiers, governed IRIs, display names, slugs, categories and domain specializations.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG, FHIR CareTeam, GitHub Team, Microsoft Graph team, SCIM Group and Schema.org SportsTeam all treat the team as an identifiable named entity before membership is enumerated. Classification is required because those sources disagree on whether a team is an OrganizationalUnit, a CareTeam, a sports Organization, a Scrum Team or an access group.

layers.name: Identifiers and names
layers.description: Canonical identifiers, external identifiers, names, slugs, descriptions and alternative labels for the team.

findings.name: Canonical team identity
findings.description: A Team instance requires a durable identifier that survives rename. Priority is the identifier assigned by the authoritative master system of record, then a governed IRI, then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. Dates, display names and slugs are not identifiers.

questions.text: What identifier does the authoritative master system assign to this team, and which system is that master?
What governed IRI, SCIM id, FHIR identifier or Dimension UUID or ULID identifies this team when no master identifier is available?
Which external identifiers must remain constant as the team record is updated or propagated between systems?
Is a generated slug, mail nickname or display name being treated as identity despite being derived from a changeable name?

data_elements.name: Master-system team identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the system of record, such as GitHub team id, Microsoft Graph team id shared with the group, FHIR CareTeam.id or SCIM Group id.

data_elements.name: Governed IRI
data_elements.description: HTTP IRI for the team when published as linked data, typically an org:Organization or org:OrganizationalUnit individual.

data_elements.name: External identifiers
data_elements.description: Business or clinical identifiers that remain constant as the record is updated and propagated, including SCIM externalId and FHIR identifier.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or governed identifier exists. A date is not an identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is reference data: identifiers, IRIs and UUID or ULID values. No separate artifact is required beyond the team record itself.

findings.name: Names, slugs and descriptions
findings.description: Human-readable names, alternative labels, generated slugs or mail nicknames, and optional descriptions that distinguish like teams without serving as identity.

questions.text: What is the preferred human-readable name of the team, and in which language or locale is it expressed?
What alternative names, generated slugs, mail nicknames or notations exist, and which system derives them from the preferred name?
What description or comment distinguishes this team from similarly named teams, such as red versus green trauma teams?
Who is authorized to change the team name, description or profile picture?

data_elements.name: Preferred name
data_elements.description: Primary display name, corresponding to skos:prefLabel, FHIR name, GitHub name, Microsoft displayName or SCIM displayName.

data_elements.name: Alternative names
data_elements.description: Trading, colloquial or historical names using skos:altLabel or equivalent.

data_elements.name: Slug or mail nickname
data_elements.description: URL or mention handle derived from the name, such as a GitHub slug or Microsoft mailNickname. Not an identifier.

data_elements.name: Description
data_elements.description: Optional description; Microsoft Graph limits description to 1024 characters.

artifacts.name: Team profile page
artifacts.description: The team page or profile from which name, description and picture are maintained, such as a GitHub team page.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Team master identifier plus profile resource locator from the host organization directory

layers.name: Kind and profile
layers.description: Classification of the team by kind, category, specialization and domain profile, without implying legal-entity type.

findings.name: Team kind and category
findings.description: A Team should be classified so co-existing teams can be differentiated, for example care-plan versus episode team, visible workplace team versus secret team, or Scrum Team versus sports team. ORG leaves classification open to profiles.

questions.text: What kind or category of team is this, using the local controlled vocabulary and any aligned standard code?
Which classification scheme or profile constrains allowed kinds, and is the scheme legal-form, service, clinical category or product-method?
Which co-existing categories apply at once, such as longitudinal care team and encounter team, and how are they disambiguated?
Is this team also a legal Organization, as Schema.org SportsTeam may be, or only an OrganizationalUnit with no legal personality?

data_elements.name: Team kind code
data_elements.description: Code for team kind or category, such as FHIR CareTeam.category or a local workplace vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Legal personality flag
data_elements.description: Whether the team is recognized as a FormalOrganization or legal sports organization rather than an internal unit.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Kind and category are coded classification values and flags stored on the team record; they do not require a separate artifact.

findings.name: Specialization and domain profile
findings.description: Optional specialization that selects domain behaviours, such as Microsoft class team, education specialization, Scrum Team operating rules, or Schema.org sport and team gender.

questions.text: What specialization, template or method profile applies, and which unique behaviours does it unlock or constrain?
If this is a sports or other domain team, what sport, discipline or domain label applies?
Does an extended gender label, mixed-team flag or class-team setting apply to this team as a whole?
Which operating rules, such as Scrum no-hierarchy or GitHub secret-team no-nesting, are inherited from the chosen profile rather than locally overridden?

data_elements.name: Specialization code
data_elements.description: Microsoft Graph specialization or equivalent method profile.

data_elements.name: Sport or domain
data_elements.description: Schema.org sport text or URL, or another domain label.

data_elements.name: Creation template
data_elements.description: Template from which the team was created, when the platform records one.

artifacts.name: Team template or profile binding
artifacts.description: Record of the template or method profile used at creation, such as a Microsoft teamsTemplate reference.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Template master identifier plus team identifier

bundles.name: Purpose, mandate and operating model
bundles.description: Why the team exists, what subject or goal it serves, and which size, autonomy and accountability constraints govern how it works.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG requires a purpose beyond the set of members. FHIR records why a care team exists and who it is for. Scrum binds a team to one Product Goal and collective accountability. ISO 30400 frames a group of people with functions, responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve objectives.

layers.name: Purpose and subject
layers.description: Defining purpose, remit, subject of care, product goal or sporting competition membership.

findings.name: Defining purpose
findings.description: The team has a common purpose or reason for existence independent of particular members. Purpose may be recorded as org:purpose, FHIR reason, Scrum Product Goal or a charter text.

questions.text: What is the defining purpose, remit or Product Goal of this team, independent of who currently belongs to it?
If a coded reason exists, why does the team exist, and to which condition, mission or objective does that reason refer?
Is the stated purpose still valid for the current interval, or has the team been re-purposed without a change event?
Which organization or person authorized this mandate, and under what instrument?

data_elements.name: Purpose statement
data_elements.description: Text or concept describing why the team exists, aligned to org:purpose or Scrum Product Goal.

data_elements.name: Reason
data_elements.description: Coded or referenced reason the team exists, as in FHIR CareTeam.reason.

artifacts.name: Team charter or purpose instrument
artifacts.description: Charter, remit, Product Goal statement or authorizing note that records why the team exists.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative document identifier of the issuing organization; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID

findings.name: Subject, goal or sport context
findings.description: Optional subject of care, product, event or sporting affiliation that the team is for, including teams formed before a subject is identified.

questions.text: Who or what is the team for: a patient, a group, a product, a sporting competition, or an event that has no subject yet?
Which league, club, sports organization or competition is this sports team a member of?
May this team exist without a subject, as a code-blue or emergency response team, and under what trigger is a subject later bound?
Does this team share a Product Goal, backlog or owner with sibling teams after a size-driven split?

data_elements.name: Subject reference
data_elements.description: Patient, Group, product or other subject the team serves. Cardinality 0..1 because FHIR allows event teams before a subject is identified.

data_elements.name: Member of organizations
data_elements.description: Sports organizations, leagues or other bodies this team belongs to.

data_elements.name: Shared product goal
data_elements.description: Product Goal shared when multiple Scrum Teams form around the same product.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject, competition membership and shared-goal links are references on the team record, not a separate artifact class.

layers.name: Operating constraints
layers.description: Size, self-management, cross-functionality and collective accountability constraints that some profiles impose.

findings.name: Size, autonomy and accountability
findings.description: Scrum Teams are typically 10 or fewer, cross-functional and self-managing, with collective accountability for a Sprint Increment and no internal hierarchy. Other team kinds do not inherit those constraints. ISO 30400 still requires functions, responsibilities, authorities and relationships.

questions.text: What minimum or maximum size constraint applies, and is it a Scrum typical bound, a local policy or unconstrained?
Is the team self-managing, meaning members decide who does what, when and how, or does an external manager assign work?
Is the whole team collectively accountable for outcomes, or are outcomes split by role, post or reporting line?
Must the team hold all skills needed to create value in one cycle, and which skill gaps are currently accepted?

data_elements.name: Maximum size
data_elements.description: Upper bound on team size where a profile or policy sets one; Scrum typically 10 or fewer.

data_elements.name: Current headcount
data_elements.description: Count of owners, members and guests or equivalent summary.

data_elements.name: Self-managing flag
data_elements.description: Whether the team internally decides who does what, when and how.

data_elements.name: Collective accountability flag
data_elements.description: Whether the entire team is accountable for the valued outcome each cycle.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Size and autonomy constraints are policy flags and counts on the team record unless a named charter artifact already records them.

bundles.name: Organizational placement and nesting
bundles.description: How the team sits inside or across organizations, including containing and managing organizations, multi-organization participation, parent-child nesting and the collaboration-versus-unit boundary.
bundles.rationale: Vercy known relations state that an Organization contains Team instances. W3C ORG models unitOf and hasUnit, GitHub models a single parent team, Microsoft binds a team to a tenant group, and FHIR allows several managing organizations plus onBehalfOf. Scrum forbids internal sub-teams, which conflicts with nested-team systems.

layers.name: Host organization
layers.description: Containing organization, managing organization, tenant and multi-organization participation.

findings.name: Containing and managing organization
findings.description: Most workplace teams are units of one FormalOrganization or Microsoft tenant. FHIR separately records managingOrganization as the organization responsible for the care team. GitHub teams exist only inside an organization.

questions.text: Which Organization instance contains this team, and is the team a unit with meaning only inside that organization?
Which organization is responsible for managing the team, if that is different from the containing organization?
Which tenant, directory or provisioning domain hosts the team record?
Must every member already belong to the containing organization, as GitHub requires, or may outsiders participate?

data_elements.name: Containing organization
data_elements.description: Reference to the Organization of which this team is a unit or child.

data_elements.name: Managing organizations
data_elements.description: Organizations responsible for the team, as in FHIR managingOrganization.

data_elements.name: Tenant identifier
data_elements.description: Microsoft Entra tenant or equivalent directory that hosts the team.

artifacts.name: Organization chart extract
artifacts.description: Chart or directory extract showing the team as a unit of a containing organization.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Containing organization master identifier plus chart version timestamp in RFC 3339

findings.name: Multi-organization participation
findings.description: Participants may act on behalf of another organization, and membership may include organizations or nested teams, producing multi-organization teams without making the team itself a consortium.

questions.text: For each practitioner or agent, on behalf of which organization do they participate?
Which organizations are members of the team, as opposed to merely managing it?
Are the members predominantly persons, or is this actually an OrganizationalCollaboration whose members are organizations?
What policy exception or agreement allows cross-organization membership when the default is single-organization membership?

data_elements.name: On behalf of
data_elements.description: Organization of a practitioner participant, constrained in FHIR to Practitioner members.

data_elements.name: Member organizations
data_elements.description: Organizations participating as team members rather than as the containing unit.

artifacts.name: Cross-organization participation agreement
artifacts.description: Agreement that authorizes a person or organization to participate in a team hosted by another organization.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuing organization master identifier plus agreement identifier

layers.name: Nesting and collaboration boundary
layers.description: Parent-child team structure, inherited membership, and the boundary against OrganizationalCollaboration.

findings.name: Parent-child and team-of-teams
findings.description: GitHub allows one parent team and many children; child teams inherit parent permissions; listed members of a parent include child members but those members are not direct parent members. Secret teams cannot nest. Scrum forbids sub-teams and instead splits oversized teams into multiple teams sharing a Product Goal. SCIM Groups may nest Groups. FHIR CareTeam may have another CareTeam as a participant.

questions.text: What is the parent team, if any, and does this team have exactly one parent as in GitHub or an open unit hierarchy as in ORG?
Which child teams exist, and do their members count as inherited members of this team for listing, mentions or permissions?
Is nesting forbidden because this is a Scrum Team, a secret team, or another profile that rejects sub-teams?
When size or complexity requires change, should the team split into sibling teams sharing a goal rather than adding a child team?

data_elements.name: Parent team
data_elements.description: Reference to a single parent team where the platform uses a tree, such as GitHub parent.

data_elements.name: Child teams
data_elements.description: Teams nested under this team.

data_elements.name: Nesting forbidden
data_elements.description: True when the chosen profile or privacy class, such as Scrum or GitHub secret, forbids parent or child teams.

artifacts.name: Team hierarchy snapshot
artifacts.description: Point-in-time tree of parent and child teams used to audit inherited permissions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Containing organization identifier plus snapshot observation time in RFC 3339

findings.name: Collaboration versus unit boundary
findings.description: A Team that is an OrganizationalUnit lives inside one organization. A collaboration among organizations is org:OrganizationalCollaboration or FOAF Project and should not be modelled as this Team unless individual membership and a team purpose are also present.

questions.text: Is this team recognized only inside a containing organization, matching OrganizationalUnit, or does it have standing of its own?
Are the primary members persons and other agents, or organizations playing roles in a venture?
Should this record be reclassified to OrganizationalCollaboration or Project rather than remaining a Team?
What non-containment links to other organizations exist, such as funding or supply relationships that must not be mistaken for unit hierarchy?

data_elements.name: Unit-only flag
data_elements.description: True when the team has recognition only inside a containing organization and is not a legal entity.

data_elements.name: Linked organizations
data_elements.description: Arbitrary org:linkedTo relationships that are not containment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The collaboration-versus-unit decision is a classification and set of references on the team record.

bundles.name: Membership, posts and accountabilities
bundles.description: Who is on the team, in what state and for what interval, how membership is invited or synchronized, and how the team is composed through posts, roles, accountabilities and leadership.
bundles.rationale: Composition is the operating core of Team. W3C ORG separates memberOf, n-ary Membership with Role and memberDuring, and Post independent of holder. FHIR allows role-only participants and nested CareTeams. GitHub and Microsoft use member or maintainer and owner, member or guest. Scrum uses accountabilities rather than job roles. Positions remain a sibling model.

layers.name: Membership records
layers.description: Member identity and kind, interval, state, inheritance, invitations, IdP synchronization and dynamic rules.

findings.name: Member agent and kind
findings.description: A member may be a person, practitioner, related person, patient, organization, nested team, SCIM User or SCIM Group. GitHub restricts members to organization members and excludes outside collaborators. FHIR may list the patient only when they have a role other than subject of care, and may omit member when only a role is known.

questions.text: Who are the direct members of the team, and what agent kind is each: person, organization, nested team, guest or other?
Which participants are known only by role because the person is not yet assigned, as in a draft care team?
Are guests, patients, family members or other non-organization members allowed, or does policy require organization membership?
If a member is itself a Group or CareTeam, is membership flattened for operations, or kept as a nested agent?

data_elements.name: Member agent
data_elements.description: Reference to the person, organization, team or other agent who is a member.

data_elements.name: Member kind
data_elements.description: Type of member resource, such as User, Group, Practitioner, RelatedPerson, Organization, CareTeam or Guest.

data_elements.name: Direct membership flag
data_elements.description: True when the agent is a direct member rather than inherited from a child team.

artifacts.name: Membership roster
artifacts.description: Current and historical list of members with kind and direct or inherited status.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Team master identifier plus roster observation time in RFC 3339

findings.name: Membership interval, state and inheritance
findings.description: Membership is time-qualified. ORG uses memberDuring; Schema.org OrganizationRole uses startDate and endDate; FHIR participant coverage may be a Period or Timing; GitHub exposes state and inherited. Listed parent-team members may include child-team members who are not direct members.

questions.text: Over what interval is each membership valid, recording start and end as RFC 3339 date-times with offset or Z?
What is the membership state, such as active, pending invitation, inherited or ended?
When is the member generally available to this team, if coverage is a repeating timing rather than a single period?
For this membership change, what was the event time versus the observation or ingestion time?

data_elements.name: Membership start
data_elements.description: Start of membership interval as RFC 3339 timestamp with offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Membership end
data_elements.description: End of membership interval as RFC 3339 timestamp with offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Membership state
data_elements.description: State such as GitHub active, or equivalent pending, ended or inherited.

data_elements.name: Inherited membership
data_elements.description: True when membership is inherited from a child team rather than direct.

artifacts.name: Membership record
artifacts.description: N-ary membership including agent, team, role or post, interval and state, corresponding to org:Membership.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative membership identifier from the master directory; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID

findings.name: Invitation, synchronization and dynamic rules
findings.description: Membership may be pending invitation, locked to an identity-provider group, or computed from a dynamic membership rule. Local writes may be forbidden while synchronization is active.

questions.text: Which invitations to join the team are pending, who invited them, and when were the invitations created?
Is membership synchronized from an identity-provider group, and does that block local add or remove operations?
Is membership computed from a directory rule, and is processing on or paused?
Who may add or remove members when local writes are allowed: organization owner, team maintainer, team owner or another role?

data_elements.name: IdP synchronization enabled
data_elements.description: True when GitHub team synchronization or equivalent binds membership to an identity-provider group.

data_elements.name: Dynamic membership rule
data_elements.description: Rule that determines members when the associated group uses dynamic membership.

data_elements.name: Local write blocked
data_elements.description: True when API or local membership changes are rejected because an IdP owns membership.

artifacts.name: Team invitation
artifacts.description: Pending invitation to a person to join the team, including inviter, role and creation time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Invitation master identifier from the host organization; else Dimension UUID

layers.name: Posts, roles and leadership
layers.description: Reusable posts, played roles, Scrum accountabilities and leadership designations used to compose the team without duplicating the Position model.

findings.name: Posts, positions and assignments
findings.description: A Post exists independently of the incumbent and is the join to WM-ORG-004. A team may have posts even when vacant. Assignment of a holder is a time-qualified hold relation, not identity of the post.

questions.text: Which posts or positions exist on this team, including vacant posts that currently have no holder?
Who currently holds each post, and may a post be held by more than one person at once?
What is the assignment interval for each holder, with RFC 3339 start and end?
Is the agent a member of the team ex officio because they hold a post, rather than by personal appointment?

data_elements.name: Post or position
data_elements.description: Reference to a WM-ORG-004 Position or org:Post that exists on the team independently of the holder.

data_elements.name: Post holder
data_elements.description: Agent currently holding the post.

data_elements.name: Ex officio membership
data_elements.description: True when team membership follows from holding the post rather than personal appointment.

artifacts.name: Team post register
artifacts.description: Register of posts on the team and current or historical holders.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Team identifier plus post master identifier from the position register

findings.name: Roles, accountabilities and leadership
findings.description: Abstract roles, Scrum accountabilities, GitHub member or maintainer, Microsoft owner member or guest, FHIR participant role, and sports athlete or coach, plus headOf leadership. These are not job descriptions.

questions.text: What role, accountability or participation type does each member hold on this team?
Who is the formal head, product owner, Scrum Master, team owner, maintainer or coach, and is that a unique seat?
If this is a Scrum Team, are the three accountabilities present, and is internal hierarchy asserted despite the Guide forbidding it?
What reporting line exists among members, if any, and does it conflict with a self-managing profile?

data_elements.name: Role or accountability
data_elements.description: Abstract role, FHIR participant role, GitHub member or maintainer, Microsoft owner member or guest, or Scrum accountability.

data_elements.name: Head of team
data_elements.description: Agent who is org:headOf the team.

data_elements.name: Sports performance role
data_elements.description: Athlete versus coach distinction for sports teams.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Roles and accountabilities are coded attributes of membership or leadership references; they become artifacts only when a separate job description exists, which is out of scope.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, time and history
bundles.description: Operational status of the team, the interval it covers, substantial change events such as merger or restructure, and end states including archive, entered-in-error and deletion.
bundles.rationale: FHIR CareTeam status and period, Microsoft createdDateTime and isArchived with archive and unarchive operations, GitHub created_at and updated_at, Schema.org foundingDate and dissolutionDate, and W3C ORG ChangeEvent aligned to PROV-O together define a lifecycle that is richer than create-update-delete.

layers.name: Status and interval
layers.description: Current operational status and the intended or actual existence interval of the team.

findings.name: Operational status
findings.description: Status values in use across sources include proposed, active, suspended, inactive, entered-in-error, archived or read-only, owner-only class membership, and migration mode. These are alignments, not a merged code system.

questions.text: What is the current operational status of the team, and which status system is being used?
Is the team archived read-only, limited to owners, or in migration mode, and who may still write?
Which status transitions are allowed from the current state, including unarchive, reactivate or entered-in-error correction?
Does this status act as a modifier, as FHIR status does, so that other fields must be interpreted differently?

data_elements.name: Status code
data_elements.description: Operational status such as FHIR proposed, active, suspended, inactive, entered-in-error, or Microsoft isArchived.

data_elements.name: Archived flag
data_elements.description: True when the team is in read-only archive state.

data_elements.name: Migration mode
data_elements.description: True when the team is being used for migration and is not yet available for ordinary posting.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Operational status is a coded field on the team record; transition history is captured under change events when a distinct event is required.

findings.name: Existence period and change events
findings.description: The period the team covers is distinct from record created and updated times. Substantial change such as merger, rename with new identity, or restructure is an org:ChangeEvent linked to PROV-O, producing a new URI when the resulting team is distinct.

questions.text: What period is the team intended to cover, with RFC 3339 start and end distinct from created and last-modified timestamps?
When was the team founded or dissolved, if those civic or sporting dates apply in addition to operational period?
What change events created, merged, split or restructured this team, and which original and resulting team identities are linked?
Did the team keep its identifier through the change, or was a new URI required because the result is a distinct organization?

data_elements.name: Team period start
data_elements.description: When the team came or is intended to come into effect.

data_elements.name: Team period end
data_elements.description: When the team ended or is intended to end.

data_elements.name: Created at
data_elements.description: Record creation timestamp from the platform, not a substitute for team period start.

data_elements.name: Change event
data_elements.description: Reference to an org:ChangeEvent or equivalent merger, split or restructure activity.

artifacts.name: Team change event record
artifacts.description: Record of a substantial change such as merger, split, rebrand or restructure, including original and resulting identities and PROV interval.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Change-event identifier from the organization register; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID

layers.name: End states
layers.description: Archive, unarchive, entered-in-error, clone, delete and retention of membership history.

findings.name: Archive, error and deletion
findings.description: Microsoft archive puts a team in read-only state and unarchive restores it; clone copies team and group. FHIR entered-in-error marks a record that should not have existed. Delete of a Microsoft team also deletes the associated group. Retention of membership history after deletion is not specified by these sources.

questions.text: Is the team archived, entered in error, or otherwise an end state that is not a clean dissolution?
Is the requested operation archive, unarchive, clone, mark entered-in-error, or irreversible delete of team and associated group?
After archive or delete, what retention period applies to the team record and membership history, and who is the retention authority?
Who is authorized to archive, unarchive, clone or delete the team?

data_elements.name: End-state code
data_elements.description: Archive, entered-in-error, dissolved or deleted.

data_elements.name: Associated group fate
data_elements.description: Whether delete of the team also deletes the bound directory group.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Retention duration for the team record and membership history after an end state. Recorded as a duration because primary sources do not fix a universal period.

artifacts.name: Archive or deletion record
artifacts.description: Operation record for archive, unarchive, clone or delete, including actor and event time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Platform async-operation or audit identifier; else Dimension UUID

bundles.name: Access, location, provenance and quality
bundles.description: Visibility and sensitivity, entitlements granted to the team, member capability settings, site and contact, schedule, provenance and interoperability mappings.
bundles.rationale: GitHub and Microsoft make visibility and entitlements first-class. ORG and Schema.org locate teams at sites. FHIR adds team-level telecom. SCIM, FHIR, ORG and Schema.org are alignments, not claimed conformance. SCIM also requires privacy care when propagating membership.

layers.name: Visibility and entitlements
layers.description: Who can see the team, how sensitive it is, what resources it can access, and what members are allowed to do inside it.

findings.name: Visibility, privacy and sensitivity
findings.description: GitHub contrasts visible and secret teams, with API values secret and closed; secret teams cannot nest and still leak their name if @mentioned. Microsoft visibility defaults to Public and classification must match a tenant-preconfigured sensitivity label. People outside the organization cannot view GitHub teams.

questions.text: What is the visibility or privacy class of the team, and which vocabulary is in use: GitHub secret or closed, GitHub visible or secret, or Microsoft Public or Private?
What sensitivity or business-data classification applies, and does it match a preconfigured directory label?
Who can discover, view or @mention the team, and does a mention of a secret team reveal its name?
What privacy duty applies when distributing membership lists across provisioning domains, as SCIM warns?

data_elements.name: Visibility code
data_elements.description: Privacy or visibility class of the team.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Tenant directory sensitivity label or equivalent.

data_elements.name: Discoverability audience
data_elements.description: Who may find the team in search or mention it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Visibility and sensitivity are coded policy fields on the team record.

findings.name: Entitlements and member capabilities
findings.description: Teams hold permissions on resources such as repositories, inherit child-team access from parents, and expose member, guest and messaging capability settings. Entitlements are relationships to resources, not the team itself.

questions.text: Which resources can the team access, at what permission level, and are those entitlements inherited by child teams?
What may ordinary members create, update or delete inside the team, such as channels, apps, tabs or connectors?
What may guests do, and how does that differ from member and owner capabilities?
What exception grants a person or child team broader access than the team default, and who authorized it?

data_elements.name: Team entitlements
data_elements.description: Permissions the team holds on repositories or other resources.

data_elements.name: Member capability settings
data_elements.description: Settings for whether members may create channels, add apps and similar actions.

data_elements.name: Guest capability settings
data_elements.description: Settings for guest actions inside the team.

artifacts.name: Team entitlement grant
artifacts.description: Grant of a permission on a resource to the team, including inheritance notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Resource master identifier plus team identifier plus grant identifier

layers.name: Location and contact
layers.description: Sites, home location, team-level contact points and operational schedules.

findings.name: Site, contact and schedule
findings.description: ORG locates organizations at Site and persons at basedAt or location. Schema.org SportsTeam has homeLocation and address. FHIR CareTeam has team-level telecom that applies to all members. Microsoft Graph exposes a schedule of shifts for the team. Virtual-only teams are a gap in these primary sources.

questions.text: Where is the team based, including primary site, home location, address or basedAt site?
What telephone, email or other contact points apply to the team as a whole rather than to individual members?
What shift or availability schedule exists for the team, if any?
Is the team virtual with no physical site, and if so how is location recorded without inventing a site?

data_elements.name: Primary site
data_elements.description: org:hasPrimarySite or equivalent place reference.

data_elements.name: Home location
data_elements.description: Schema.org homeLocation or address for a sports or other placed team.

data_elements.name: Team contact points
data_elements.description: Contact details that apply to all members.

data_elements.name: Team schedule
data_elements.description: Reference to a shift schedule for the team.

artifacts.name: Team schedule
artifacts.description: Schedule of shifts or availability for the team when the platform maintains one.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Schedule master identifier bound to the team identifier

layers.name: Provenance and interoperability
layers.description: Where the team record came from, how complete it is, and how it aligns to external standards without false conformance claims.

findings.name: Provenance, evidence and interoperability
findings.description: Record provenance includes creator, source system, created and last-modified times, SCIM meta version and notes. Interoperability is alignment to ORG, FHIR CareTeam, GitHub Team, Microsoft Graph team, SCIM Group, Schema.org SportsTeam, Scrum Team and FOAF Group. Conflicts are recorded rather than merged.

questions.text: Which system authored the current team record, at what created and last-modified times, and which version token applies?
What evidence, notes or annotations support the stated membership, purpose and status?
Which external types is this instance aligned to, and is any alignment claimed as conformance?
What quality issues are open, such as missing purpose, role-only draft members, IdP sync drift or conflicting hierarchy rules?

data_elements.name: Source system
data_elements.description: System that authored or last provisioned the team record.

data_elements.name: Version token
data_elements.description: SCIM meta.version or equivalent concurrency token.

data_elements.name: Aligned external types
data_elements.description: External classes or resources this instance is aligned to, without implying conformance.

data_elements.name: Notes
data_elements.description: Comments made about the team, as in FHIR note.

artifacts.name: Interoperability mapping record
artifacts.description: Record of aligned external types, identifiers in those systems, known conflicts and whether conformance is claimed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Team identifier plus mapping-record UUID assigned by the Dimension

functions.name: Register team
functions.description: Create a Team instance with identity, preferred name, containing organization where required, and optional purpose, privacy and parent.
inputs: optional purpose, privacy, parent, template and identifiers
preconditions: Caller is permitted to create teams in the host organization
Parent team, if supplied, exists and is nestable
Name and privacy combination is valid for nested versus secret teams
effects: A Team record exists with master or Dimension identity
Creator may be recorded as maintainer or owner without a separate add

functions.name: Assign membership
functions.description: Add, update or end a membership, including role or accountability, interval, invitation and inherited versus direct status.
preconditions: Team is visible to the actor and not IdP-sync locked
Member is an allowed kind for the team profile
Local writes are permitted
effects: Direct membership becomes active, pending or ended
Inherited listings of parent teams may change when child membership changes

functions.name: Compose via post
functions.description: Attach a reusable post to the team and optionally assign a holder for an interval, without creating the post definition.
preconditions: Referenced post exists in the Position model
Assignment interval uses RFC 3339 timestamps if present
effects: Team composition includes the post even if vacant
Holder may become an ex-officio member

functions.name: Nest or reparent team
functions.description: Set, change or clear a parent team, or split an oversized team into sibling teams sharing a goal.
preconditions: Secret or Scrum profiles are not asked to nest
New parent is not a descendant of the child
Actors have maintainer or owner rights on both teams when required
effects: Child inherits parent entitlements where the platform so defines
Direct versus inherited membership listings change
A Scrum-style split shares Product Goal rather than creating hierarchy

functions.name: Change team status
functions.description: Move a team among proposed, active, suspended, archived, unarchived, migration-complete or entered-in-error states.
preconditions: Requested transition is allowed from current status
Archive or error states are not used as silent deletes
effects: Modifier status changes how other fields are interpreted

functions.name: Grant team entitlement
functions.description: Grant, inherit or revoke a permission held by the team on a resource.
preconditions: Actor may manage access on the resource
Child-team inheritance implications have been reviewed
effects: Team members and, where defined, child-team members gain or lose resource access

functions.name: Provision from external group
functions.description: Create or update a Team from a SCIM Group or identity-provider group, or bind an existing team to that group.
preconditions: Group displayName and members are available
Privacy agreements for cross-domain personal data have been considered
effects: Team membership is sourced from the external group
Local membership writes may be blocked

functions.name: Resolve effective members
functions.description: Compute the effective member set, distinguishing direct, inherited, guest, role-only and nested-group members at an observation time.
inputs: inclusion flags for inherited guests and nested groups
preconditions: Caller may read membership of the team
effects: No write; returns an observation of membership at the stated time

functions.name: Record change event
functions.description: Record a substantial merger, split, restructure or identity-changing rename using original and resulting team identities.
preconditions: Resulting identity is distinct when ORG requires a new URI
Event times are RFC 3339 with offset or Z
effects: Original and resulting teams are linked through a ChangeEvent
Provenance may be further described with PROV-O terms

composition.purpose: A Team is typically an OrganizationalUnit or other contained instance of an Organization; the Organization CONTAINS Team relation is stored here as a reference to the containing or managing organization rather than duplicating legal-entity attributes.
A Team is composed through reusable posts or positions and time-qualified assignments so that vacant posts and ex-officio membership remain expressible without merging Position into Team.
Members, heads, coaches, athletes, maintainers and owners are agents whose master identity lives outside this model.
Primary site, home location and basedAt relations locate a team without embedding a gazetteer.
Clinical CareTeam is an alignment for status, subject, period, role-only participants, nested CareTeam members and managingOrganization, not a claimed FHIR profile.
SCIM Group is the provisioning alignment when a team is exchanged as an identity group with nested User or Group members.
SportsTeam alignment covers athlete, coach, sport, OrganizationRole intervals and possible legal-organization standing of a club team.
Scrum Team alignment covers size, self-management, cross-functionality, Product Goal and accountabilities, including the conflicting no-sub-team rule.
FOAF Group is aligned only as a generic class of Agents; Team requires a purpose beyond grouping and must not collapse into FOAF Group, Organization or Project.
Keep multi-organization ventures whose members are organizations in a sibling collaboration or project model rather than as Team.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the master system of record for Team identity in the adopting organization, for example HR directory, GitHub organization, Microsoft Entra, or clinical CareTeam server.
Bind containing Organization identifiers to WM-ORG-001 and post identifiers to WM-ORG-004 rather than minting parallel org or post records.
Publish the local team-kind vocabulary, privacy classes and status map as a profile, because ORG, FHIR, GitHub, Microsoft and Scrum do not share one code system.
State whether nested teams, secret teams, guests and IdP synchronization are enabled, because those choices change cardinality and write rules.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension namespace under the adopting organization's governed URI, for example {org-namespace}/team/{id}, and treat GitHub team id, Microsoft group id, FHIR CareTeam.id and SCIM Group id as master-system identifiers mapped into that namespace. Do not use slugs, mail nicknames or dates as namespace keys.
registry_links: WM-ORG-001 Organization via CONTAINS and unitOf or managingOrganization
WM-ORG-004 Position via COMPOSE through posts and assignments

canonicalization_rules: Prefer master-system identifier, then governed IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID; never canonicalize on name, slug or date.
Treat preferred name plus language tag as the canonical label; keep slugs and mail nicknames as derived projections.
Record membership as n-ary records with agent, team, role or post, direct or inherited flag and interval, rather than as an unordered identifier list.
Keep team period, membership interval, event time and ingestion time as separate RFC 3339 timestamps.
Map external types as alignments with conflict flags; do not rewrite a Scrum Team into a nested GitHub tree or a SportsTeam into an OrganizationalUnit without an explicit profile choice.
patch_rules: Patch membership independently of team identity and of post definitions.
Reject local membership patches when IdP synchronization owns membership.
Status patches that archive, suspend or mark entered-in-error must not silently delete history.
Parent changes must reject cycles and secret-team nesting.
Name changes may regenerate slug projections but must not change identity.
compatibility_rules: A reader must accept teams with no members, including FHIR role-only drafts.
A reader must accept either a single parent, an open ORG unit hierarchy, or a no-nesting Scrum profile.
Unknown specialization or category codes must be preserved, not dropped.
Absence of legal-entity attributes must not be interpreted as completeness of an Organization record.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier of the team, membership, post, grant or change event
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event times and observation or ingestion times use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; never use a date as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts append an UTC RFC 3339 observation time and a monotonic sequence to the team master identifier, for example team/{id}/roster/{observation-time}/n.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Roster, hierarchy, charter, invitation, grant and change-event artifacts must include the team identifier, issuer or source system, event time and a content hash or version token so that later patches cannot silently rewrite history.

policies: Default deny read of secret or private team membership to non-members and non-owners; visible workplace teams may be listed to organization members according to the host directory.
Membership lists are personal data when they identify persons; cross-domain SCIM or IdP propagation requires a recorded privacy agreement.
Do not claim FHIR, SCIM, ORG or Scrum conformance unless a named profile and evidence are attached to the instance.
Nested entitlement inheritance must be audited before a parent-child link is created, because child teams inherit parent resource permissions in GitHub-like systems.

read: Resolve canonical identity then names, status and containing organization
Resolve effective members only if the caller is in the visibility audience
Return inherited versus direct membership flags rather than flattening without notice
create: Require preferred name and a master or Dimension identifier
Require containing organization when the profile is a workplace unit or GitHub-like team
Optionally accept purpose, parent, privacy, template and initial maintainers
update: Allow name, description, purpose, status, parent, visibility and capability settings by authorized maintainers
Route membership changes through assign-membership rather than rewriting a bag of ids
Block membership updates when IdP synchronization is enabled
delete: Prefer archive or inactive over hard delete when history is required
If delete is used, record associated group fate and retention hold
Do not delete reusable posts in WM-ORG-004 when removing them from a team

roles.name: Team registrar
responsibilities: Ensure containing organization and kind are set
Refuse secret-team nesting and identity-as-slug errors

roles.name: Team maintainer or owner
responsibilities: Add or remove members when local writes are allowed
Request parent changes and review inherited entitlements

roles.name: Organization owner or directory administrator
responsibilities: Manage IdP synchronization and tenant classification labels
Archive, unarchive or delete teams and bound groups

roles.name: Membership subject
responsibilities: Receive invitations and appear on rosters according to visibility rules
Exercise or decline guest or member capabilities

roles.name: Care or product lead
responsibilities: Hold headOf, Product Owner, Scrum Master, coach or clinical lead accountability as the profile requires
Keep purpose or Product Goal current

roles.name: Agent reader
responsibilities: Read AGENTS.md then specification, storage, interface and process URLs
Operate only within declared visibility and sync constraints

access.default_rule: Deny read of membership and secret-team existence to callers who are not organization owners, team owners or members; allow listing of visible teams to organization members where the host directory so provides.
exceptions: Break-glass clinical or security access to a CareTeam or secret team must be time-bounded, logged and tied to a named incident
IdP administrators may mutate membership in the identity provider even when the Team API rejects local writes
Public sports-team facts such as name, sport and listed athletes may be published without implying access to workplace membership rosters
audit_requirements: Log create, membership add and remove, parent change, entitlement grant, archive, unarchive, clone and delete with actor, event time and observation time
Log IdP-sync failures and rejected local writes
Retain audit records at least as long as the team membership history retention period

coverage.claim: This model covers Team as a purpose-bearing collection of agents, typically contained by an Organization and composed through memberships and optional posts, aligned to W3C ORG, HL7 FHIR CareTeam, GitHub Team, Microsoft Graph team, IETF SCIM Group, Schema.org SportsTeam, the 2020 Scrum Guide, ISO 30400 organization vocabulary and FOAF Group, without claiming a unified conformance profile.

checklist.notes: Master-system id, governed IRI, FHIR identifier, SCIM id and externalId, and Dimension UUID or ULID are in canonical-team-identity; names and slugs are explicitly non-identifiers.
FHIR status, Microsoft archive and migration, clone, entered-in-error, dissolution and ChangeEvent are modelled; hard-delete retention remains a local policy.
Containing and managing organizations, parent-child teams, members, posts, headship, memberOf sports bodies and onBehalfOf links are modelled.
Team period, membership memberDuring or OrganizationRole dates, coverage timing, created and updated timestamps, and separate event versus ingestion time are required as RFC 3339.
Source system, version token, notes, PROV-aligned ChangeEvent and interop mapping records are included.
Managing organization, tenant, team owners, maintainers and mandate authority are included; legal ownership of a FormalOrganization is out of scope.
FHIR participant invariants, secret-team nesting bans, Scrum no-hierarchy checks, IdP write locks and status-as-modifier interpretation are included as validation questions.
Visibility classes, sensitivity labels, entitlements, member and guest capability settings, default-deny membership read and break-glass exceptions are included.
Archive versus delete, associated group fate, retention period and legal hold are asked; no primary source supplies a universal retention duration.
Alignments to ORG, FHIR CareTeam, GitHub Team, Microsoft Graph team, SCIM Group, Schema.org SportsTeam, Scrum Team and FOAF Group are explicit, with conflicts recorded.
Direct, inherited, guest, organization, nested-team, role-only, invited, synchronized and dynamic membership are covered.
ORG purpose, FHIR reason, Scrum Product Goal and ISO 30400 objectives-bearing group are covered.

known_omissions: ISO 30400:2022 public pages define organization but do not expose a Team term in the freely retrievable text, so Team-as-HR-object remains an alignment gap.
Schema.org has SportsTeam but no generic Team type.
Crew, watch and shift-based operational teams in aviation and maritime domains lack a primary source in this pass.
Military fireteam, squad and TO&E structures were not sourced.
Committees, boards and works councils were excluded rather than modelled.
IPTC Sport Schema Club and TeamMembership (noted in secondary discovery) were not fetched as primary.
ISO 21502 project-team vocabulary was not fetched.
Virtual-only teams without a Site have no primary location pattern beyond a gap flag.
GDPR or other regional retention schedules for membership rosters are not specified by the team sources used.
SAFe Agile Release Train and other named team-of-teams methods beyond Scrum's split guidance were not sourced.
conflicts: Scrum Guide 2020 forbids sub-teams and hierarchies; GitHub nested teams, ORG unit hierarchy, SCIM nested Groups and FHIR nested CareTeam allow them.
Schema.org SportsTeam is an Organization and may be a legal club; W3C OrganizationalUnit is not a legal entity.
Microsoft Graph team is 1:1 with a Microsoft 365 group and is also a collection of channels; GitHub Team is not an organization and cannot include outside collaborators.
GitHub Docs say visible versus secret while the Teams API uses privacy secret versus closed.
FHIR allows role-only participants and non-organization members including patients and related persons; GitHub requires organization members.
SCIM Group is an access-control grouping and does not require a purpose; this model requires purpose for Team.
Scrum replaced roles with accountabilities that are not job descriptions; ORG Role, FHIR participant.role and GitHub maintainer remain role-like.
Microsoft default visibility is Public; GitHub default for a non-nested team is secret.
regional_assumptions: FHIR CareTeam is treated as the clinical projection, which is strongest in jurisdictions that adopt HL7 FHIR, including US Core profiles not made mandatory here.
GitHub and Microsoft Graph represent widely deployed Anglo-American workplace directories, not statutory public-administration team registers.
ISO 30400 is an international vocabulary; local labour-law definitions of team or crew may differ and were not surveyed.
Schema.org sports gender and mixed-team text values follow Schema.org's own non-enumerative guidance and are not a legal sex classification.
adversarial_checks: If a record has members but no purpose, it should be classified as Group or access list rather than Team, matching ORG and the FHIR Group versus CareTeam boundary.
If members are only organizations, the record should move to OrganizationalCollaboration or Project rather than Team.
If identity is a slug or founding date, the record fails the identity priority rule.
If a Scrum Team is stored with parent-child hierarchy, a conflict flag is mandatory rather than silent nesting.
If IdP synchronization is on, local membership writes must fail rather than drift.
If a secret team is nested, the instance is invalid against GitHub's primary rule even if another profile allows hierarchy.
If Microsoft delete is requested, the associated group fate must be explicit so that directory identity is not destroyed by accident.
